theory.intro: Many real-life problems combine or compare fractions of the same whole. When the denominators match, add or subtract the numerators only.
facts: Fractions of the same whole with the same denominator have **same-size parts**.
Keep the **denominator the same** — only the numerators change.
Read what is known and what is asked. Add to combine amounts; subtract to remove an amount or find a difference. To find a starting amount, undo the change.
steps: Read what is known and what is asked. Decide whether to combine, remove, compare or work back to a starting amount.
Add or subtract the numerators and keep the common denominator.
Simplify the answer if possible and include the units when needed.

workedExamples.question_text:
Two ribbons measure $\frac{2}{9}$ m and $\frac{4}{9}$ m.
(a) Find their total length.
(b) A third ribbon measures $\frac{1}{9}$ m. Find the total length of all three ribbons.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $\frac{2}{9}+\frac{4}{9}=\frac{6}{9}=\frac{2}{3}$ m
(b) $\frac{2}{9}+\frac{4}{9}+\frac{1}{9}=\frac{7}{9}$ m
Add the numbers of ninths and keep the denominator $9$.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) A jug contains $\frac{13}{15}$ L. After $\frac{7}{15}$ L is poured out, how much is left?
(b) Another jug has $\frac{6}{15}$ L left after $\frac{7}{15}$ L is poured out. How much was in it at the start?
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Subtract the amount poured out.
$\frac{13}{15}-\frac{7}{15}=\frac{6}{15}=\frac{2}{5}$ L
(b) Add the amount poured out back to the amount left.
$\frac{6}{15}+\frac{7}{15}=\frac{13}{15}$ L
Both questions mention an amount left, but they ask for different amounts.

workedExamples.question_text: Red paint covers $\frac{11}{16}$ of a board and blue paint covers $\frac{5}{16}$. How much more of the board is covered by red paint than blue paint?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Subtract to find the difference.
$\frac{11}{16}-\frac{5}{16}=\frac{6}{16}=\frac{3}{8}$
Red paint covers $\frac{3}{8}$ more of the board.

workedExamples.question_text: Mia reads $\frac{10}{19}$ of a novel on Monday and a further $\frac{3}{19}$ on Tuesday. What fraction is still unread?
workedExamples.solution_text:
First find the fraction read.
$\frac{10}{19}+\frac{3}{19}=\frac{13}{19}$
The whole novel is $\frac{19}{19}$.
$\frac{19}{19}-\frac{13}{19}=\frac{6}{19}$
The unread fraction is $\frac{6}{19}$.

workedExamples.question_text: A group raises $\frac{17}{22}$ of its target on the first day and $\frac{8}{22}$ on the second day. By what fraction of the target does the total exceed the target?
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\frac{17}{22}+\frac{8}{22}=\frac{25}{22}$
One whole target is $\frac{22}{22}$.
$\frac{25}{22}-\frac{22}{22}=\frac{3}{22}$
The total exceeds the target by $\frac{3}{22}$ of the target.

workedExamples.question_text: A walker travels forward $\frac{21}{28}$ of a route, then walks back $\frac{18}{28}$ of the route. How far forward is the walker from the starting point, as a fraction of the route?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Subtract the distance walked back from the distance walked forward.
$\frac{21}{28}-\frac{18}{28}=\frac{3}{28}$
The walker is $\frac{3}{28}$ of the route forward from the starting point.

foundation.question_text:
Nia walks $\frac{2}{9}$ km before lunch and $\frac{4}{9}$ km after lunch.
How far does she walk altogether?
A jug contains $\frac{7}{10}$ L. Sam pours out $\frac{3}{10}$ L. How much remains?
Two ribbons measure $\frac{3}{8}$ m and $\frac{2}{8}$ m. What is their total length?

A book is $\frac{9}{12}$ read.
Yesterday $\frac{4}{12}$ was read.
What fraction was read before yesterday?

Separate parts of a board are painted: red paint covers $\frac{5}{11}$ of the board and blue paint covers $\frac{3}{11}$.
What fraction is painted?

A trail is $\frac{8}{10}$ km long.
Eva has completed $\frac{5}{10}$ km.
How much farther must she go?

development.question_text:
At a fair, $\frac{4}{15}$ of tickets were sold online and $\frac{7}{15}$ at the gate.
What fraction were sold altogether?

A tank was $\frac{13}{16}$ full and then $\frac{5}{16}$ of its capacity was used.
What fraction remains?

Mika read $\frac{3}{10}$ of a novel on Monday and $\frac{4}{10}$ on Tuesday.
What fraction is left unread?

A garden has $\frac{6}{12}$ planted with herbs and $\frac{5}{12}$ with flowers.
How much more is herbs than flowers?

Three teams use $\frac{2}{9}$, $\frac{4}{9}$ and $\frac{1}{9}$ of a field.
What fraction do they use in total?

A recipe needs $\frac{9}{8}$ cups of stock.
You have $\frac{5}{8}$ cup.
How much more is needed?

mastery.question_text:
A cyclist rides $\frac{5}{12}$ of a route in the morning and $\frac{4}{12}$ in the afternoon.
She then rides back $\frac{2}{12}$ of the route.
What net fraction of the route has she travelled forward?

A class collected $\frac{7}{10}$ of its target on Monday and another $\frac{5}{10}$ on Tuesday.
By what fraction did it exceed one whole target?

A container lost $\frac{3}{14}$ of its capacity, then another $\frac{4}{14}$.
It now holds $\frac{5}{14}$.
What fraction did it hold at first?
